title: Dynamic hybrid INT8/FP8 staging with dequant hedging to minimize decode tail latency
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Reduce 95th/99th percentile decode latency for interactive streaming by combining INT8 fast-path kernels with FP8 fallbacks in a lightweight staging layer and a dequant hedging policy that mitigates dequant overhead spikes.

Background: Current runtime selects between INT8 and FP8 kernel variants per-layer at dispatch time, but we observe tail spikes when dequantization operations contend with attention and KV-cache activity during decode. In workloads with variable sequence prefixes and per-head sparsity variance, eager dequantization increases memory traffic and causes tail latency regressions.

Proposal: Implement a 'staging lane' inside the runtime dispatcher that: 1) starts requests on INT8 kernels where safe, 2) opportunistically stamps per-head fidelity scores from a lightweight telemetry sampler, 3) defers full dequantization until a hedging threshold is crossed (time or divergence in logits), and 4) provides a fast-path fallback to single-layer FP8 execution for heads that exceed fidelity loss budget. The staging lane is a thin arbitration layer that avoids wholesale per-token dequant until necessary, reducing KV-cache thrashing.

Key components:
- Staging dispatcher: token-aware dispatch that tags microbatches with a staged state (INT8, hedging, or escalated-FP8).
- Hedging policy: tunable thresholds (logit divergence, per-head entropy delta, wall-time) and a small credit-based timer to allow transient deviations without escalation.
- Microkernel variants: lightweight INT8 attention that writes compact shadow accumulators, and a fast single-layer FP8 escalation path with minimal copy semantics.
- Telemetry hooks: per-request microtraces, per-head fidelity metric, and a bounded sampler (1-2%) to compute hedging signals without high overhead.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end 95th percentile decode latency reduced by >= 15% on conversational benchmark (avg prefix 64, decode length 32) compared to current INT8-first baseline.
- No more than 2% quality (ROUGE/BLEU/LL) regression vs full-FP8 baseline on evaluation prompts due to staging; when regression exceeds threshold, hedging should escalate to FP8 and remove regression.
- CPU/GPU memory traffic reduction measured in NVLink/mm copy patterns for hedged workloads by >= 10%.
- Feature is feature-flagged and can be enabled per-customer or per-model variant in console.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Hedge oscillation causing thrashing between INT8 and FP8. Mitigation: credit-based timer and hysteresis thresholds; offline simulation harness for oscillation detection.
- Risk: Telemetry overhead increases latency. Mitigation: low-sample-rate bounded sampler + off-path aggregation.
- Risk: Complex fallback interactions with existing rollout policies. Mitigation: expose clear metrics and safe defaults; start behind experiment flag.

Test plan: microbenchmarks for microkernel throughput, end-to-end decode bench against conv-sim dataset, unit tests for hedging state transitions, chaos tests with synthetic KV-cache pressure, and compare outputs on evaluation prompt sets.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile decode latency improvement >= 15% vs INT8 baseline
Quality regression <= 2% vs FP8 baseline unless escalated
Memory traffic (copy patterns) reduced >= 10% for hedged workloads
Configurable feature flag with per-customer enablement in console
implementation_notes: Add 'staging_state' tag to request context (string: INT8|HEDGE|FP8)
Introduce low-cost per-head fidelity sampler (1-2% of requests) emitting to runtime telemetry topic
Create microkernel: int8_attention_shadow_accum that writes compact accumulators to preallocated slab
Implement credit-based hedging timer with configurable decay and hysteresis
Expose knobs in model catalog: hedging_enabled, hedging_thresholds, hedging_timer_ms
